title: Herb Morand, Lucien Johnson, Bigfoot Bill Phillips and Kid Clayton
summary: He recalls playing with trumpeter Herb Morand and brother, Lucien Johnson, Bill Phillips and Kid Clayton, one of his first bands.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: What about, uh, Herb Moran? Did you ever know him?
Herb Moran? I was a play with him. Oh, yeah? Yeah. Herb Moran trumpet player? Yeah. Yeah. I'd play with his brother's drummer, McGee.
Yeah.
Yeah.
I knew them both.
I'd play with all the people, man. Oh, I love his playing, man.
Who was in the band?
Yeah?
Who was in the band with you and Herbert and McGee?
No, man. I can't remember. That's a long camera room, man. I can't remember that.
What did Lucian Johnson play?
That's what?
Oh, okay.
He died in California.
And you played with him?
Yeah, Lucian Johnson, too.
And, uh, did he have a band ever?
No, he had a band. Never.
And what about Bigfoot Bill, but Phillips?
That's who he used to play with.
Yeah. Lucian used to play with him?
Yeah, all of us used to play with Bigfoot Bill.
Oh.
Bill Phillips. Uh-huh.
He died, huh? He died. Yeah, he died. He was out of somebody that played a trick on him. He died. They buried him, anyway. Yeah. They buried him?
Yeah.
What about Kid Clayton? Kid Clayton, he died, too. Did you play with him ever? Yeah, man.
That was one of my first new bands. I started out with one of the other ones.
Good bands, boy. That guy could play.

Very young, boy. Could he play blues? Play anything, man. He was a good band boy. That guy could play. Very young boy. Could he play blues? Play anything man. He could play anything. The damnest man I ever played with in my life was Lee Collins.
